articleTitle: A New Hybrid Approach to Dynamic Pricing Categorization Using Deep Learning and Neutrosophic
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: appropriate dynamic pricing categorization of clothing plays a significant role in commercial applications, particularly in the rapid development of daily fashion. In this paper, a new clothing price hybrid approach is introduced based on market demands, the fashion season, and certain clothing criteria. This hybrid approach is made up of three different stages. The first stage consists of using the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to enhance the dataset by generating more images. The second step involves using a Generative Adversarial Denoising Network (DGAN-Net), a U-Shaped Network (D-U- NET), and an autoencoder network to suppress noise in fashion images. Furthermore, the free-form images are used in accordance with the Peak Signal Noise Ratio (PSNR) and the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) measures. In the second phase, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used to recommend the closest clothes to the trendy clothing stock. In the final stage, a neutrosophic multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approach is used to dynamically sort products according to various criteria such as seasonality, product quality, own stock range, tax price, degree of comfort, etc. The hybrid approach achieves values of (93.61, 93.21, 92.66, and 92.64) in the recommendation process using CNN and (93.14, 92.64, 92.14, and 92.18) in enhancing the dataset using GAN in terms of accuracy, dice score, recall, and precision, respectively. The results also show the efficiency of the modified models for removing noise when compared with other available methods for removing noise according to the values of PSNR and SSIM for different levels of noise.

articleTitle: Social Listening Using Machine Learning and NLP to Make Sense of Frontline Employees Experiences and Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The recent politico-civil unrest around the world, coupled with COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns, brought to the fore the challenges frontline employees experience as they navigate the stress from unprecedented market, social, and cultural disruptions, crises, and transition. Frontlines is the study of interactions and interfaces between an organization and its customers at the point of contact that promote, facilitate, or enable value creation and exchange [1]. The employees managing these points of contact are the frontline employees (FLEs). Social media is the first platform where frontline employees share their opinions, experiences, and concerns. While reducing the misinformational effect of social media, this paper uses Machine Learning (ML) to enhance social listening and capture trends and patterns of frontline stress and consequences [2]. For the purpose of making sense of frontline experiences, this research uses Reddit, the fifth largest social and somewhat technical discussion board where users anonymously share and discuss information. The use of machine learning and natural language processing helped us better understand the stress imposed by the customers, coworkers, management, and local policies and FLE perceptions and actions in response to those.

articleTitle: Workspace Mobile Application Finder Based on Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Finding the best-fit workspace – collection of heterogeneous places to meet, work or study – is considered a problem for clients who cannot determine the availability of the spaces at a specific moment. The availability of spaces in workspaces is another problem because it needs real time communication with each workspace. Therefore, a system that searches in a registered workspace to find the nearest available workspace using a mobile app developed by flutter. A backend Laravel system that communicates with the workspace software to find a real time state is introduced in this paper. In addition, software is built that manages workspace and keeps track of its availability. The main merit of this software is accepting the request of the first solution software to give a real time state of the available spaces in its workspace. Discern a workspace to fall under a certain label allows us to recommend workspaces to clients easily based on machine learning ML) techniques.Our main approach involved is using traditional ML methods, where we train and build a model based on a dataset and use that model in order to predict a rating that a client might give a workcspace. A client is able to give a rating from 1 to 5 stars meaning we have 5 separate labels that we need to classify a workspace under. Since we need to predict a discrete label from 1 to 5, this is a classification problem. So, therefore a classification-based approach, where we use ML models' classification in order to classify a workspace between 5 labels each representing a possible rating that a client could rate a workspace. Furthermore, separate applications that can communicate are developed in this paper. In addition, a platform is performed that offers both workspaces and clients a means of interacting with each other. In this paper, a system that records all workspace-related data, including name, location, and lists of available workers, is constructed. This gives customers a way to register and reserve a space or a seat at the selected workspace as well as a way to keep track of all their interactions. It is observed that by generating a synthetic dataset that represent the relation between certain features and rating and by using a random forest model, we are able to predict the rating group of a workspace. This is achieved utilizing ML techniques with a classification accuracy of 0.79 and a precision and recall values of 0.787 and 0.790, respectively, giving much better scores compared to other models we tested.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Spectrum Sensing for Cognitive Radio System Using Energy Detection over Different Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The radio spectrum must be used most effectively by cognitive radio systems. One of the challenges that cognitive radio systems must overcome the detection of main users over the spectrum. We employ sensing techniques such as energy detection, matching filter detection, and cyclostationary feature detection to solve this issue. This paper focuses on energy detection approach for spectrum sensing, for both Rayleigh fading channel and Rician fading channel. The probability of missed detection and the probability of false alarm for each channel were compared using MATLAB software. It is found that, depending on certain parameters like SNR, the performance of an energy detector varies when used with various channel types.

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a complication of diabetes caused by the high blood sugar levels damaging the back of the eye and block the blood vessels from feeding the retina. DR is usually not noticed in the early stages, when it does not have any obvious symptoms. Symptoms typically become noticeable when the condition is more advanced. A possible sudden total loss of vision and blindness may occur. Therefore, an early detection and treatment of the disease is required to reduce the risk of complications, and avoid the risk of blindness. In this paper, a computer-aided diagnosis tool based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) is proposed for the early detection of DR and classification of its severity. Transfer learning is utilized to extract deep features from the last fully connected layers and average pooling layers of the ResNet50 architecture model. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves 81.4% accuracy on the APTOS dataset fundus images.

articleTitle: A comparative Analysis of ensemble methods and their efficiency in the classification of ‘HIT AND RUN’ cases in an imbalanced dataset (Traffic Crashes) with and without using "Synthetic minority oversampling technique"
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In some cases of developing a predictive model for a classification problem, the distribution of classes is skewed, meaning a majority of the training samples belong to a single class and a very small number of samples belong to a minority class. If Machine Learning techniques are applied directly to such data sets, it may result in a model which either ignores the minority class as a whole or gives less importance to the samples belonging to the minority class. Such datasets are often called imbalanced datasets. There are multiple ways to deal with these problems some include Random Over Sampling, Random Under Sampling, Threshold value tuning, one class classification to find the outlier, etc. One such technique is called the "Synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE)". In this paper we are going to analyze the efficiency of ensemble methods for the classification of imbalanced datasets with and without using SMOTE. The Dataset used for this purpose is an open-source Traffic crashes dataset available on the Chicago data portal. The target variable for our study is the "HIT_AND_RUN_I" column available in the dataset. This is a dichotomous variable that has 2 valid values. "Y" for the cases that are of positive outcomes as in "HIT_AND_RUN_I" = yes. "N" for the cases that are of negative outcomes as in "HIT_AND_RUN_I" = No.

articleTitle: CIRAJ: An Extended IoT Reference Architecture for Gamified Smart Classrooms
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The gamification of classroom environments is introduced to enhance content delivery, student engagement, and assessment during the educational process, which is recently becoming a popular approach. This involves making use of IoT-based systems to monitor and control the classroom, as well as to help teachers to manage students’ behaviors and engagement. Currently, such gamification systems are designed in an ad hoc manner without taking into consideration the proper IoT reference architecture. This can lead to inadequate designs, hindering such systems’ development, integration, maintenance, and evolution. To overcome such a problem, this paper proposes CIRAJ, an extended IoT reference architecture for Gamified Smart Classrooms (GSC). CIRAJ extends the SANAD IoT reference architecture by adding layers to handle the required gamification, cognition, and decision-making functionalities required by GSC systems. A comparison between existing GSC systems using CIRAJ is provided, showing that CIRAJ is comprehensive enough to handle current GSC requirements.

articleTitle: A Novel Computational Method for Predicting DNA Methylation Sites within WGBS of Chromosome Y with WGS Data and Illumina Array Data
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: DNA methylation is a critical component of epigenetics that plays a crucial role in cell specification and the development of various human diseases. It also has the potential to assist in early disease prediction and treatment planning. While cost-effective methods such as Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip (450K arrays) are commonly used for DNA methylation measurement, they only cover a small portion of the CpG sites in the human genome. On the other hand, whole genome bisulfite sequencing(WGBS) covers a larger portion of CpG sites but is expensive and time-consuming. Previous studies have developed computational methods for predicting DNA methylation with high accuracy. However, these methods rely on genomic or epigenetic features obtained from costly and challenging experiments. To address this issue, a novel method has been developed for predicting methylation sites that overcomes the limitations of previous approaches. The method utilizes machine learning algorithms such as Generalized Linear Model (GLM), Decision Tree and Random Forest (RF) which use K-mer and atomic number as sequence features extracted from the whole genome sequence(WGS) of chromosome Y. These sequence features are then combined with the 450k features obtained from 450k array data of IMR90 cells and adrenal cells. The IMR90 cells are used as training data, while the adrenal cells serve as testing data. The study revealed that the random forest algorithm outperformed the other algorithms, achieving a balanced accuracy of 66%, a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROCAUC) of 73% and a recall area under the curve (PRAUC) of 93%. The outstanding performance of random forest, has made it a popular choice for regression analysis in estimating the beta value of each CpG site in WGBS. Overall, this method demonstrates potential in predicting DNA methylation sites and provides valuable insights into epigenetic regulation and its implications for human health and disease.

articleTitle: Smart Autonomous IoT Agricultural Monitoring System for Banana Agriculture in Egypt
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Banana agriculture in Egypt faces many challenges due to global climate change and a lack of water resources. The requirement for reliable and optimized irrigation techniques is vital in light of the current severe weather conditions and water resources. So, a new concept introduced is smart agriculture, in which IoT sensor networks afford information about agriculture fields and make precise decisions based on user inputs and sensor readings. In this paper, a novel solar-powered IoT intelligent autonomous agricultural monitoring system is proposed that benefits from advances in the latest developed technologies such as IoT, microcontrollers, and Wireless Sensor Networks. The proposed system’s main goal is to use evolving technology for monitoring environmental conditions to enhance the efficiency of crops. The proposed system can monitor humidity, temperature, and soil moisture, which will impact the efficiency and farming cost of banana crops, by maintaining controlled sensors with microcontroller boards that have inferior power dissipation to establish a wireless sensor network that has an irrigation unit working autonomously to take actions either to irrigate the farm or not based on pre-programmed water level thresholds. The proposed system is most likely suitable due to savings in water consumption, powering by harvesting solar energy, and low construction costs.

articleTitle: Impacts of Smartphones’ Distraction on Driving Behavior: Naturalistic Data Collection Using A Smartphone Application
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The high number of fatalities, injuries, and property damage caused by traffic collisions, which are mainly attributed to human errors such as distraction and fatigue, has led to the development of various initiatives to address distracted driving. Real-time driver distraction countermeasures have been developed to prevent or reduce distraction before it occurs and to provide early and clear warnings to the driver in case of distraction. The use of inertial measurement units (IMUs) of smartphones, which can recognize drivers' distractions and performance patterns, has been suggested as a possible way to identify distractions during driving. This paper reports on the development of an Android application that collects IMU data from smartphones to analyze drivers' distraction and performance while driving. The paper also discusses the strengths and weaknesses of the application and its outputs which is a cornerstone for the next steps of the future research.

articleTitle: Analyzing User Interest Detection in Web sites: A Bimodal Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In the world of online navigation, understanding user interaction is crucial. We introduce a unique bimodal model for seeing and analyzing user interest in web adverts in this work. Our innovative method employs real-time camera data, combining face expression analysis and gaze tracking. The presented system utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to understand more about user emotions while interacting with advertisements. Furthermore, we have built a gaze tracking algorithm that catches and saves gaze coordinates, as well as associated facial emotions, in a CSV file. Surprisingly, our study indicates that the upper center of the homepage receives the most visual attention, while the bottom right quadrant receives the least. With respect to Euclidean distance, the greatest distance measured was 21.4, resulting in the highest path similarity of 42.9%. Furthermore, about 18% has some common screen starting points and 22% terminate at the same screen endpoint. These findings provide an important foundation for improving advertising strategies and optimizing user experience in the changing world of web navigation.

articleTitle: Stairs Gait Cycle Trajectory Prediction and Phase Segmentation Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: It is challenging to control an active prosthesis to achieve normal gait, especially in complicated activities such as climbing stairs. For that, activity recognition, phase segmentation, and trajectory generation are critical parameters in the development of an active prosthesis. In this study, an embedded system deployed controller based on multi-deep learning models is developed. Three sequential models are developed: the first to classify current activity focused on ascending stairs, the next to the current gait phase classifier, and finally kinetic trajectory regression based on the results from the previous models. The models were trained based on IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) readings of the shank (independent of the motion of the foot) 100ms or a window of five readings. Different CNN and MLP models were developed for each step, and their precision was tested. In the first step, MLP could classify stairs up by 91% and down by 75%, with an overall accuracy of 89%, while CNN could classify stairs up by 91% and down by 74%, and an overall accuracy of 92%. In the second step, the ascending gait was divided into seven segments (toe off, foot clearance, mid-swing, foot placement, foot contact, weight acceptance and forward continuation). MLP and CNN achieved almost the same overall classification accuracy as 73%. In the last step, the models predict the trajectory of the gait 200ms ahead or a window of ten readings. CNN achieved a better correlation coefficient of 0.983 compared to 0.933 for MLP and a better root mean square error of 0.121 (deg/s) compared to 0.246 (deg/s) for MLP. Overall, CNN achieved better results, but is computationally heavier than MLP.

articleTitle: Integration of Advanced Automated Systems Utilizing Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Industrial automation has been always associated with the increase need of manufacturing productivity, enhancement of product quality, increase the safety of the operational environment, and quick response to changing of consumer demands. This paper introduces and utilizes modern principles underlying the design and operation of advanced automation systems, based on distributed control system (DCS) structure, using commercial components provided by Siemens brand. The main contributed objective of this paper is to experimentally introduce a simple and effective way of integration between two different (old and new) generations of industrial automated systems using a single platform (TIA portal) with different communication protocols. Also, the paper suggests an industrial internet of things (IIoT) structure to connect the industrial programmable controllers (PLCs) through mobile application for remote access and visualization. The work in the paper is then extended to involve a simple artificial intelligence (AI) based technique, as an example for product quality assurance, using available components and programming packages, as a step ahead towards validation of industry 4.0 concepts.

articleTitle: Detecting Sarcasm in Arabic Text Using Model Soup of Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In this paper, we address the sarcasm detection problem in Arabic text using a variant of model soups. Sarcasm is a form of irony that occurs when there is an unexpected difference between the literal meaning of an expression and its intended meaning. Through this discrepancy, the speaker expresses their position towards a prior proposition, often in the form of surface contempt or derogation. In this paper, we used the Arabic iSarcasmEval dataset provided by SemEval-2022 task 6 for sub-task A. Sub-task A is to determine if the text is sarcastic or not. In our solution, we utilized the model soup approach. Our model soup is composed of fine-tuned deep learning based models leveraging MARBERT pretrained language model, by averaging the weights of different models fine-tuned with various hyperparameter configurations to solve the sub-task A associated with the dataset. The proposed solutions outperformed the winning model in sub-task A. The uniform and the greedy soups achieved 0.6926 and 0.6682 F1-sarcastic on the testing set, respectively, while the F1-sarcastic for the winning ensemble model in Arabic sub-task A was 0.5632.

articleTitle: Adaptive Pyramid with Tree-map Visualization
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: An Image is worth a thousand words. This is an extremely expressive idiom that shows how efficiently and effectively a person can retrieve the information or data in a way that seems easy for all people. The same concept applies when it comes to digital media! In this paper, an information will be shown as drawn figures that will enable better visualization for any image. The proposed technique for image hierarchical display and visualization depends on a hybrid technique of adaptive pyramid with tree-map visualization techniques. This method takes the advantage of the hierarchical shape of the adaptive pyramid with advantage of visualization using tree-maps. The experimental results on various types of images are presented and analyzed showing an accuracy above 90%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection and Segmentation Using Identity Generative Adversarial Network and Attention Residual U-Net
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Early detection of brain tumors contributes effectively to the journey of the diagnosis. The segmentation of brain tumors helps clinicians in the detection and examination of brain tumors. Augmentation preprocessing leads to a highly accurate segmentation process. This paper presents a framework that contains two main stages: (1) augmenting the MRI using a modified version of the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) called Identity Generative Adversarial Network (IGAN), and (2) segmenting the Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) image using attention residual U-Net. The Augmentation of MRI contains two different steps. The first step is that the framework uses a modified model IGAN to solve the problems mentioned in the different types of GANs. The modified model contains three different modifications to improve the performance of GAN. The first modification is to add a non-linear identity block to the architecture to make it easier for the model to fit complex data types and cut down on the time it takes to train. The second modification is to smooth the standard GAN loss function by using a modified loss function and label smoothing, and the third modification is to use mini-batch training to let the model use other examples from the same mini-batch as side information to improve the quality and variety of generated images. The second step is about using the IGAN in the augmentation process. The second main stage is about using the attention residual u-net for segmentation MRI. The framework achieves high accuracy in the augmentation process and also in the segmentation process using IGAN and attention residual U-Net, respectively. The IGANs achieve an Inception score of 13.6 and a Freshet Inception Distance of 46.2 in the Augmentation Step and also achieve 96.46 and 96.68 in Dice Score and Accuracy, respectively. The experiments have shown the efficiency of the used models in both augmentation and segmentation when compared with other models doing the same tasks.

articleTitle: Scheduling Linear Workflows with Various Levels of Privacy Requirements in a Fog – Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In complex distributed computing architectures, such as fog and cloud frameworks, there are workloads which consist of jobs characterized by different levels of privacy requirements. In this type of computing environment, it is of paramount importance to employ privacy-aware scheduling schemes, so that appropriate execution of the applications is ensured, and the desired Quality of Service (QoS) is achieved. Based on this direction in this research we study privacy-aware scheduling techniques for linear workflow (LW) applications in a fog-cloud computing platform. Only the fog resources are considered suitable for processing LW jobs with privacy requirements. The remaining LW jobs may run on either cloud or fog resources. A new scheduling technique is employed which applies approximate computations for the sake of jobs requiring to ensure privacy of their data. It is compared with the case where no approximate computations can be tolerated. Extensive simulation experiments are carried out for the evaluation of their performance. The simulations reveal useful insights into how different levels of approximate computations set dynamically at run time affect the performance of the system in each one of the investigated cases.

articleTitle: MyHealthDigest: A Smart-Driven Medical Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Covid-19 was the biggest motivator, leading to thousands of field closures. In particular, the healthcare domain was the most critical field. Using remote communication tools to advance clinical and public health practice is known as mobile health (mHealth). Mobile phones, virtual personal assistants, patient tracking apps, and other wireless gadgets are examples of portable smart devices. Due mainly to the widespread adoption of mobile technologies worldwide, mHealth technologies are gaining much attention. In this paper, we propose a novel industrial application, "MyHealthDigest", which offers a smooth experience for patients to keep track of their health duties. In particular, it provides smart-driven features in motion capture, intelligent medical scanning, and further valuable health tracking and awareness features.

articleTitle: Hybrid Framework for Early Detection of Multiple Sclerosis through MRI Segmentation: A Multi-Layer Preprocessing and Modified Residual Attention U-Net Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a disease whichattacks the immune system. Early detection and diagnosis the MS helps the clinicians in the journey of the analysis and diagnosis. Segmentation means dividing the slice into different portions for simplifying the process of analysis and examination. The framework contains two main stages; the first stage is the multi- layer preprocessing which contains removing noise using the modified convolution neural network and augmentation step using the latent diffusion model. The second stage in the framework is about segmentation the MRI using the modified residual attention U-Net. The frame work achieves 14.89 and 38.36 in inception score and Freshet inception distance in augmentation process using the latent diffusion model. The modified CNN also achieves 43.15, 40.36, 35.26 and 31.68 Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) value for level of noise (0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 075). The residual attention U-Net achieves (96.12, 96.37, 96.15 and 96.16) values for dice score, accuracy, precision and recall respectively. The experiments have done prove the efficiency of the augmentation, removing noise and segmentation when compared with other method for doing the same tasks. The experiments also shows the enhancement of the segmentation process after applying the multi-layer preprocessing.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Computer Vision Techniques for Traffic Signs Recognition in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The popularity of self-driving vehicles has been steadily increasing due to advancements in technology. These vehicles, often referred to as autonomous vehicles, rely on a combination of sensors, cameras, and artificial intelligence to operate. Cameras have multiple applications in autonomous vehicles, including traffic sign detection and processing. This study aims to compare the performance of three computer vision techniques - SIFT (Scale Invariant Feature Transform), ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF), and CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) - on the same data set using precision, recall and F1-Score as metrics. The experimental results of this study indicate that CNN outperforms SIFT and ORB in terms of all mentioned metrics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Remote Sensing Image Classification through Modified VGG 16: Augmentation and Missing Pixel Imputation Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Remote sensing image classification plays a crucial role in various domains, such as agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. Deep learning methods have shown remarkable performance in this field due to their ability to learn complex features. However, the limited availability of labeled data and the presence of missing pixels in remote sensing images pose challenges to accurate classification. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive framework that combines data augmentation and missing pixel imputation techniques to improve the classification performance of deep learning models. This paper presents a framework that contains three main layers the first layer is about augmentation of the remote sensing dataset using the latent diffusion model, the second layer is about imputation of the missing pixel using the reinforcement learning approach, and the third layer is about classification of the remote sensing image using the modified VGG 16. We conduct extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and compare our approach with existing methods. The results demonstrate that our proposed framework significantly enhances classification accuracy and robustness, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. The experiments also prove the enhancement of the classification accuracy after augmentation and missing pixel augmentation for different architectures of U-Net. The results also prove the efficiency of the augmentation and pixel imputation when compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Fintech Discourse on Twitter: Mapping the Evolution and Interconnections of Academic Publications
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: This study aims to explore the research of Twitter and Fintech by addressing three key questions: citation and publication structure, co-citation relationships, and keyword co-occurrence. Data from 21 papers Scopus indexes, published between 2015 and 2023, were analyzed using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and VosViewer. The findings reveal that the field is rapidly growing, with key authors like Saura J.R., Pradana M., and Breidbach C.F. leading in citations and impact. However, citation count alone does not fully capture an author’s influence, as seen in the case of Bollen J. Keywords such as "Fintech" and "Financial Markets" were found to be both popular and impactful, while emerging topics like "Machine Learning" are gaining relevance. The study provides a comprehensive view of the current research trends and influential contributors, serving as a guide for future research in Twitter and Fintech.

articleTitle: Optimized End-to-End Coiflets Discrete Wavelet Transform for Dermoscopic Images Compression
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The dramatical increase in the number of images within hospitals and for consultation emerge the need for efficient medical image compression to store and transmit them. For preserving data integrity, lossless compression is used with medical images. Accordingly, the proposed system preserves the image quality while compressing the dermoscopic images using an end-to-end optimized Coiflet discrete wavelet transform (E-EOCDWT). The particle swarm optimization (PSO) was applied to determine the optimal values of the coefficients’ threshold and the level of decomposition of Coiflet discrete wavelet transform (CDWT) with minimizing the mean square error (MSE). The proposed compression system includes three main blocks, namely CDWT and inverse CDWT; entropy encoding and decoding by Huffman coding; and PSO. The CDWT decomposes the dermoscopic images into sub-band coefficients, then these coefficients are compared to the optimal threshold value (OTS). The coefficients having values less than OTS are set to zero, and then encoded using Huffman coding, while the coefficients above OTS are quantized. The Huffman decoding is used to decode the compressed bitstream. Finally, the dermoscopic images are reconstructed by applying the inverse CDWT. The proposed E-EOCDWT method was evaluated by calculating the structure similarity index measurement (SSIM), MSE, peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR), computational time (Ct), and compression ratio (CR). It achieved 41.6 dB, 1.4, 0.86, 29 sec, and 59% of PSNR, MSE, SSIM, Ct, and CR, respectively.

articleTitle: Classifying Email Spam Using K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, and AdaBoost
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The volume of undesirable spam email messages progressively surges daily. Analyzing these spam emails manually is impractical and presents challenges in terms of categorization. This is necessary to make effective classification techniques. Machine learning (ML) approaches are the most effective means to achieve accurate spam classification among the available options. This study, therefore, thoroughly examines diverse machine learning algorithms, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), and AdaBoost, to tackle the predicament of email spam classification. The research endeavor follows a sequential process encompassing multiple stages. It commences with data collection, followed by applying preprocessing methodologies and identifying pertinent features, and culminates in deploying a machine learning algorithm. The effectiveness of the developed algorithms is also comprehensively assessed, taking into account metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC.

articleTitle: MonoLite3D: Lightweight 3D Object Properties Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Reliable perception of the environment plays a crucial role in enabling efficient self-driving vehicles. Therefore, the perception system necessitates the acquisition of comprehensive 3D data regarding the surrounding objects within a specific time constrain, including their dimensions, spatial location and orientation. Deep learning has gained significant popularity in perception systems, enabling the conversion of image features captured by a camera into meaningful semantic information. This research paper introduces MonoLite3D network, an embedded-device friendly lightweight deep learning methodology designed for hardware environments with limited resources. MonoLite3D network is a cutting-edge technique that focuses on estimating multiple properties of 3D objects, encompassing their dimensions and spatial orientation, solely from monocular images. This approach is specifically designed to meet the requirements of resource-constrained environments, making it highly suitable for deployment on devices with limited computational capabilities. The experimental results validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach on the orientation benchmark of the KITTI dataset. It achieves an impressive score of 82.27% on the moderate class and 69.81% on the hard class, while still meeting the real-time requirements.

articleTitle: Review of Challenges and Need of Artificial Intelligence for the Modern Businesses in light of Strategic Vision documents of the GCC countries
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has become increasingly important for modern businesses, with the potential to transform a wide range of industries. This review article examines the challenges and needs of AI for modern businesses in the context of the strategic vision documents of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. The article focuses on the role of AI in achieving the strategic goals outlined in the vision documents of the GCC countries, highlighting the need for collaboration between government, academia, and industry to promote the adoption and development of AI technologies. The article also examines the challenges of AI adoption, including issues related to data privacy, cybersecurity, and ethical considerations. Finally, the article provides recommendations for businesses and policymakers to overcome these challenges and harness the potential of AI technology to drive economic growth and development in the GCC region. Overall, this review highlights the importance of AI technology in achieving the strategic goals of the GCC countries and the need for continued investment and collaboration to realize the full potential of this transformative technology.

articleTitle: Hackers on the Go: Investigating Cyber Threats to Crowdsourced Mobility-on-Demand Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Mobility on Demand (MoD) has transformed transportation in smart cities, with accurate demand prediction being crucial for efficient MoD applications. Deep learning models have excelled in various domains and have been successfully applied to predict demand patterns in MoD. Leveraging diverse data sources, such as historical trip data and social media feeds, these models optimize resource allocation and service quality. However, the rise of adversarial attacks poses a threat to deep learning models. In this paper, we address the vulnerabilities in MoD systems relying on crowd-sourced data and propose a defense strategy to mitigate adversarial attacks. Our research aims to enhance the security and reliability of MoD systems, advancing the transportation industry.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In this paper, a speech emotion recognition model for Cisco phone calls is introduced. The goal of this project is to provide call centers with emotional data and performance of their agents to be able to classify voices of unheard people in any language. To achieve this goal, multiple free online datasets are used, which use a discrete emotion model, which classify emotions into a named type (e.g., happy, sad, angry). A machine learning model (CNN-BiLSTM) was trained on mel-dB spectrograms, and an accuracy of 84% on a train-test split, or 68% when testing on new datasets, which can be considered high for such a task.

articleTitle: Noise Optimized Order-Statistic Energy Pre-fitted Active Contour for Accurate Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Active contour models (ACM) are best known for their simplicity and tunability in segmenting images having complex backgrounds, random noises, intensity inhomogeneity, and irregular shapes and sizes of region of interest (ROI). These models are capable of effectively using image local and global information to segment objects in multi-modal images without the requirement of large sets of training datasets. To decrease the computational costs of ACMs, pre-fitting intensity information has become a prominent option nowadays. However, pre-fitting terms sometimes increase pre-processing time, decrease accuracy, and may cut down the noise tolerance of the model. To address these issues, this work utilizes non-linear pixel sorting to calculate local intensity descriptors and construct a second-order differential loss function. The loss function is further optimized for noise cancellation and pre-fitted in the variational framework. Therefore, the proposed design attains reduced computational overhead, better accuracy and improved noise endurance compared to recently developed and related ACMs.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Gigabit Passive and Active Optical Networks for Undetectable Signal Interception
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Recently, the ever-increasing customer demands for high bandwidth and data rates have driven the need for advanced services such as video cameras and broadband internet connectivity. Although very high-speed digital subscriber line (VDSL) technology fulfils the need for wide bandwidth, it has some limitations in offering long-range communication. In this context, the utilization of optical fibers has emerged as an alternative solution for delivering high bandwidth and data rates over extended distances. Among the various optical network options, the gigabit passive optical network (GPON) has gained popularity in Europe due to its energy-saving features and point-to-multipoint transmission mechanism. This research paper aims to investigate the performance of GPONs in terms of different transmission powers and frequencies when subjected to undetectable signal tapping. A comparative analysis is carried out between GPONs and active optical networks (AONs) with varying distances. The proposed method involves eavesdropping on the upstream and downstream signals without detection. This is achieved by employing an optical coupler with specific splitting ratios (10:90, 5:95, 2:98, and 1:99) and insertion losses (0.75 dB, 0.4 dB, 0.3 dB, and 0.25 dB). Additionally, the distance between the coupler and the optical line terminal (OLT) is adjusted to 10 km, 15 dkm, and 20 km. To evaluate the quality of the intercepted signals before and after the interception, several parameters such as the quality factor (Q-factor), bit error rate (BER), and eye height are measured using the Optisystem simulator. These parameters provide insights into the intercepted signals’ quality. Subsequently, the results obtained from the various scenarios are compared, and the optimal distance from the OLT for undetectable signal interception by users is determined.

articleTitle: Deep Learning SAR-Ship Detection Model in Complex Background for Maritime Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a crucial imaging technology, providing vital maritime surveillance data. This is essential for maritime safety, security, and operational efficiency, even in challenging conditions like darkness, clouds, or bad weather. Accurate ship detection in complex backgrounds is a key SAR challenge. This paper proposes an accurate ship detection method based on YOLOv8, using adaptive training techniques. To address the challenge of detecting smaller ships near shorelines, we employ Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fusion with Spatial Pyramid Convolution. Also, model parameters are optimized with adaptive learning rate decay for better generalization. We conduct experiments and comparative analysis with HRSID and SSDD datasets, presenting a ship detection model balancing speed and mean average precision (mAP). Our final model achieves impressive performance, surpassing state of the art with a mAP of 95.20 on HRSID and 98.81 on SSDD. Applying this technique enhances maritime security and resource management.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Unseen: Leveraging Zero-Day Attack Detection Using Unsupervised and Semi-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In the ever-evolving cybersecurity landscape, detecting unseen, zero-day attacks is both urgent and paramount. These sophisticated attacks often lack precedent, posing a challenge to conventional machine learning techniques that rely on prior knowledge and training data. This paper endeavors to detect zero-day and unseen cyber attacks using zero-shot machine learning technique, which holds the promise of identifying these attacks without any prior exposure. This work explores the effectiveness of unsupervised learning in zero-day attack detection. The experimental results demonstrate that autoencoders can identify anomalies in data, which are typically associated with zero-day attacks. When compared with other unsupervised and semi-supervised learning methods, the proposed autoencoder algorithm outperforms its competitors and achieves an accuracy of 99.9%, shedding light on its relative effectiveness in zero-day attack detection.

articleTitle: Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering based Method for Image Clustering using Restricted Boltzmann Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In various verification systems, Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) have demonstrated their efficacy in both the front-end and back-end processes. In this study, we introduce the application of RBMs to the front-end for image clustering tasks. RBMs are trained to convert images into vector-based representations. In this work, we employ the conventional bottom-up Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering (AHC) technique. To address the challenge of limited test face image data, we propose RBM adaptation to a global model. Initially, a universal RBM model is trained using all available training data. Subsequently, we train an adapted RBM model using the data from each test image. The visible-to-hidden weight matrices of these adapted models, along with the bias vectors, are concatenated and subjected to whitening to generate vector representations of face images, known as RBM vectors. These vectors effectively preserve class-specific information and are utilized in image clustering tasks. Our experimental results, conducted on two benchmark image datasets (MS-Celeb-1M and DeepFashion), demonstrate that our proposed approach surpasses well-known clustering algorithms such as k-means, spectral clustering, and approximate Rank-order.

articleTitle: A Novel Transformer-Based Approach for Detecting Anomalies in Event Logs of Process-Aware Information Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Anomaly detection in the logs generated from the Process-Aware Information Systems is a critical task to prevent failures that can harm the performance of any organization. The majority of the anomaly detection approaches applied in the business process domain are unsupervised approaches because of the lack of labeled anomaly data and Perform poorly since they have no prior knowledge of the anomalies. Furthermore, almost all of them utilize a threshold to distinguish normal process executions from anomalous ones. Therefore, they have to change the threshold each time they use it on a different test set and need to struggle to find the optimal threshold that maximizes the accuracy for all test sets. This is so inappropriate to apply in real situations. In this study, we present a new method that is based on transformers to address the low-performance limitation of the current unsupervised approaches. Additionally, we propose to utilize the logistic regression classifier to separate anomalies from the data outputted based on the transformer to avoid using a threshold and enhance detection accuracy. To assess the proposed method, we used two real life and two synthetic event logs. The experimental results showed that the proposed method outperforms six competing anomaly detection methods.

articleTitle: A Novelty Two-Layered Ensemble Framework with Hybrid Filter-Based Feature Selection for Prediction of Coronary Artery Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is one of the most healthcare serious issues due to its rising death rates in world population. Hence, the need for developing a decision support system that will help in early and accurate diagnosis of CAD is essential. Machine learning and data mining approaches have been widely researched in the field of medical domain in order to help in accurate diagnosis and fast decision making. The efficiency of any Machine learning decision support system is highly dependent on the methodology involved and the dataset features selected. In this research, we have proposed a novel two-layered ensemble framework based on various types of ensemble approaches composed over two layers that will aid in the early diagnosis of CAD. This study also introduces two novel hybrid feature selection, namely Brute Force based Recursive Feature Elimination (BF-RFE) and Brute Force based CART Feature Evaluator (BF-CARTFE) for selecting CAD dataset relevant features. The proposed framework has been evaluated using Z-Alizadeh Sani dataset. The dataset imbalancing was handled using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique and the performance is evaluated. Our experimental results show robustness and efficiency of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Skin Diseases Detection Based on Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The diagnosis of human skin illnesses is the most ambiguous and challenging discipline of science. It has been noted that most cases go unreported due to a lack of improved medical infrastructure and equipment and the difficulty of visualizing the disease. This is where the concept for the project to create the first Android mobile application of its kind came from, which would assist any doctor or patient in performing a basic skin examination to identify diseases other than just skin cancer. With our work, we hope to reduce time, money, and effort involved in online diagnosis, which has become increasingly popular, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic. Deep Learning (DL) is used in this study to build an efficient model using the DenseNet technique, which proved to be the most effective. The experimental results revealed that 87% accuracy, 83% precision, 83% recall, and 83% F1-score, which were used to evaluate the system performance, are the best outcomes that could be produced with the data collected. The software enables users to log in, drop the appropriate image for instantaneous detection from the gallery or their camera roll, and display the differential diagnosis of the lesion with percentages of each potential disease. Moreover, our proposed mobile application is introduced to cover the dermatologists in six different governorates around Egypt.

articleTitle: PSO-Based Optimization of Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic for Question Difficulty Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Educational assessment has a significant role in learning process as a tool of measuring learners' performance and evaluating the knowledge of concepts that achieves learning objectives or outcomes. To design good assessments, it is useful to have a difficulty index for each question. It represents the relative difficulty of a question within a given context or test. Knowing the level of difficulty for each question before running an exam helps to classify questions, identifying the level of challenge, and ensuring a balanced mix of questions. This paper proposes an optimal Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic model-based Particle Swarm Optimization (IT2FL-PSO) in order to predict the difficulty of multiple-choice questions (MCQs) with four options and one correct answer format. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Quadrotor Performance Based on Intelligent Control Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of different controllers for quadrotor control systems, focusing on the optimization of the Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. Three controller types are examined: conventional PD controllers, Fuzzy-like PD controllers, and an optimized PD controller. Evaluation metrics such as stability, response time, and trajectory tracking accuracy are used to assess the performance of each controller. The results indicate that the Fuzzy-like PD controller outperforms the conventional PD controller, while the optimized PD controller demonstrates superior performance compared to all others. The optimized PD controller achieves enhanced stability, reduced response time, and improved trajectory tracking accuracy. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the PSO algorithm in optimizing the PD controller parameters for quadrotor control.

articleTitle: Kinship Recognition through Stacked Self-Calibrated Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Kinship recognition is becoming an important path in the evolution of biometric recognition research. Over the past decade, notable progress has been achieved in this emerging field attracting more researchers to exploit new methods for its branches. The most common use case is facial kinship recognition with its two variants: verification and identification. In this paper, we propose a novel kinship verification network based on a self-calibrated attention model and residual blocks to expand the fields-of-view through the attention stack for producing more discriminative features. In addition, we extend our work to build a kinship identification network based on joint learning of self-calibrated verification ensembles. Experimental results on benchmark datasets are demonstrated to show the effectiveness of our proposed scheme when compared to state-of-the-art solutions on the kinship identification track.

articleTitle: Enhancing Neural Machine Translation for Languages with Limited Resources Utilizing Non-Parallel Texts : An Examination of Translation from Egyptian Dialect to Modern Standard Arabic
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Machine translation for low-resource languages poses significant challenges, primarily due to the limited availability of data. In recent years, unsupervised learning has emerged as a promising approach to overcome this issue by aiming to learn translations between languages without depending on parallel data. A wide range of methods have been proposed in the literature to address this complex problem. This paper presents an in-depth investigation of semi-supervised neural machine translation specifically focusing on translating Arabic dialects, particularly Egyptian, to Modern Standard Arabic. The study employs two distinct datasets: one parallel dataset containing aligned sentences in both dialects, and a monolingual dataset where the source dialect is not directly connected to the target language in the training data. Three different translation systems are explored in this study. The first is an attention-based sequence-to-sequence model that benefits from the shared vocabulary between the Egyptian dialect and Modern Arabic to learn word embeddings. The second is an unsupervised transformer model that depends solely on monolingual data, without any parallel data. The third system starts with the parallel dataset for an initial supervised learning phase and then incorporates the monolingual data during the training process.

articleTitle: AuthMe – A Passwordless Decentralized Authentication Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Authentication is the indispensable key process of identifying a user's identity who's using a service, traditionally using passwords. As the number of services grew, password managers have, since then, been used to manage users' passwords. Traditional centralized password managers have proven their inefficacy in securing a user's password and have failed to keep up with the newer security demands, owing to their centralized architecture and reliance on quantum-vulnerable authentication methods. In this paper, an authentication manager is proposed whose model deploys a zero-trust and zero-knowledge architecture, blockchains, hardware authentication, and quantum-proof algorithms to keep up with the modern security demands. The proposed model has eliminated the single point of failure using decentralization, utilized passkeys, and deployed quantum-proof cryptographic algorithms.

articleTitle: Towards Egyptian National HPC Grid (EN-HPCG): From Cluster to Grid Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 33rd International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The significant and crucial role of HPC in science and innovation has recently been recognized in Egypt. The Egyptian National Network for High-Performance Computing (ENHPCG) encourages the pooling of high-performance computing resources into a unified and shared pool of resources among all universities and scientific research centers. EN-HPCG aims to enable multiple HPC centers located in geographically dispersed entities/organizations to coordinate their supercomputing strategies and investments together for the benefit of scientific research in Egypt. In this paper, the architecture and the capabilities of the EN-HPCG grid will be presented. Furthermore, the grid’s performance for certain types of high-throughput computing (HTC) applications will be evaluated via the NASA Grid parallel benchmark (NGB). Grid-level performance metrics such as throughput (tasks/second), site critical length, and site speed up will be measured on a real grid testbed. The presented methodology would help other partners in the decision-making phase to join the EN-HPCG grid based on the site speedup metric. Also, profiling the current scientific workload to one of the studied applications/ benchmarks would give estimates about the expected grid performance under a particular type of application.
